kira-space.description: Take a named lease on a shared resource the user configured, such as a port, the full test suite, push or merge. Never blocks: returns held, or queued with your position. The lease is keyed to your session, so calling again keeps your place. When it frees, Kira messages your session; a headless run calls acquire_lease or lease_status again to check. Call release_lease when done. A lease ends with the session, or after 10 minutes of silence.

queue.description: Lease queue name. lease_status lists them.

kira-space.name: acquire_lease

kira-space.description: Ask the user to approve pointing your task's branch at another existing local branch; waits for the answer. Use when the task folder holds a different branch than the task shows, or you must work on another existing branch. The folder and sessions stay; git switch runs there if needed. Never creates a branch: use request_branches. Outcome: changed, denied, failed or timeout. Refused for main, integration and checked-out-elsewhere branches, and a dirty folder that needs a switch.

repo.description: Task repo: nickname, name or code repo id.

to.description: Existing local branch to work on instead.

kira-space.name: change_branch

kira-space.description: Ask the user to approve a new child task; waits for the answer. The brief is the child's first handover. Child tasks cannot create tasks. Every call waits for the user, so ask for what you need in one call. Outcome: created, denied, timeout or failed. Read results with list_tasks and task_chain; you are not woken when a child finishes.

brief.description: What the child must do, what it needs to know and what to hand back. Markdown, at most 16384 bytes.

repos.description: Repos of the child, 0 to 10. Each gets a branch slot the child names later.

base.description: Ref the child's branch starts from, such as main. Default: the repo's default branch.

repo.description: Repo: nickname, name or code repo id, from task_info.

workflow.description: Workflow id or name. It must exist and have a step.

kira-space.name: create_task

kira-space.description: Add repos to the task. Only repos registered in Kira Space can be added. An unknown repo is refused: ask the user to import it from the Git module. Never removes a repo.

repos.description: Repos to add: nickname, name or code repo id of a registered repo, from task_info. 1 to 20.

kira-space.name: declare_repos

kira-space.description: Report how this pipeline step ended. Call it exactly once, as the last action.

conflictedFiles.description: Files that still conflict, relative to the repo.

lastGitError.description: Last git error output you saw.

reason.description: Why it failed, or what you need. Required when status is not ok or needs_input.

status.description: How the step ended. done (ok). failed (not ok). needs_input when the user must decide.

summary.description: One line: what was done, what failed, or the question for the user.

tried.description: What you tried before giving up.

kira-studio.description: List closed proofs, newest first, with step count and whether an edit waits for review. With name: that proof's current steps (ordinal, description, view), for an edit. The app keeps the newest 30 not attached to a task.

name.description: Name of a closed proof. Omit to list all.

kira-studio.name: proof_list

kira-studio.description: Save proof that your work is correct. Prove functionality and behavior, not code: show what the system does (query results, responses, screenshots), not source or diffs. One call creates and closes it, and the user reviews it in a window. Steps show in order; each step's description is the explanation the user reads first. Pick each step's view for its data: table, document and keyvalue show rows; chart plots a table and shows no table, so add a table step when exact values matter; diagram draws Mermaid text; image shows a JPEG, such as a UI screenshot. Names are unique, ignoring case and outer spaces. In a Kira Space task the new proof also attaches to the task. With reason, changes a closed proof instead: a step may keepOrdinal an old step unchanged or replacesOrdinal one, an old step not listed is dropped; read ordinals with proof_list and name. An edit returns pending_review until the user accepts or rejects it. Every value is validated: a bad step rejects the call, saves nothing and names steps[i] and the limit.

reason.description: Edits the closed proof with this name: what changes and why, up to 500 characters.

data.description: table: {columns:[{name,type?}],rows:[[cell,...]]}, type number, text, boolean, temporal, json or other (inferred when omitted). document: {documents:[{id?,body:{...}}]}. keyvalue: {entries:[{field,value}]}. chart, type bar, line, area or scatter: {type,x:{type,name?},y?:{name?,unit?},stacked?,horizontal?,series:[{name,points:[[x,y],...]}]}; x.type is category (x a string label), time (ISO-8601 or epoch milliseconds) or value (number); y is a number, null for a gap; stacked: bar and area only; horizontal: bar only. Histogram: bar, one point per bucket. Time series: line or area, x.type time. Up to 20 series, 1000 categories, 20000 points (bar and scatter 1000). chart, type pie: {type,unit?,slices:[{name,value}]}, up to 50 slices, values 0 or more. diagram: {source}, Mermaid text whose first line starts with flowchart, graph, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, stateDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, erDiagram, gantt, journey, gitGraph, mindmap or timeline. No front matter, %%{...}%% directives, click lines, url(), @import or image nodes; send screenshots as an image step. Up to 20000 bytes, 1000 lines, 500 edges. Quote labels that hold punctuation: A["label (x)"]; a syntax error shows the user the parser message and your source. image: exactly one of {path} or {base64}. path is the absolute path of a JPEG on this machine; the app reads it at save, follows symlinks and stores a copy. base64 is the file's bytes, standard base64, no data: prefix. JPEG only, at most 3071 KiB, 16384 pixels a side and 16 megapixels. Inline base64 counts toward the 8 MiB request limit; pass paths for large or several images. A proof holds at most 32 MiB of stored data; an image stores about 4/3 of its file size. Limits: 10000 rows or documents, 64 KiB per cell, 4 MiB per step. Required unless keepOrdinal is set.

description.description: The explanation, shown large above the data: one terse, clear line, ideally under 120 characters, at most 200. Say what the step shows and what that proves. Required unless keepOrdinal is set.

keepOrdinal.description: Edits only: reuse the old step with this ordinal unchanged. Pass no other step field.

language.description: Highlighting for query: sql, json, shell or text. Default text.

query.description: The query or command you ran, up to 64 KiB. Shown above the data.

replacesOrdinal.description: Edits only: this step is a changed version of the old step with this ordinal.

source.description: Short label of the tool that produced the data, such as elasticsearch. Up to 64 characters.

view.description: table, document, keyvalue, chart, diagram or image. Required unless keepOrdinal is set.

summary.description: Which behavior it proves: 1-3 terse, clear sentences, up to 500 characters. Shown above the steps. New proofs only.

kira-studio.name: proof_save
